claims.statement: The F-gas Regulation prohibits use of Annex I gases with GWP of 2,500 or more for maintenance or servicing of air-conditioning and heat pumps from 1 January 2026, subject to specified reclaimed and recycled-gas exceptions through 2032.

The regulation's Annex IV includes 1 January 2027 prohibitions affecting self-contained equipment and split air-to-water systems up to 12 kW that use fluorinated gases at or above specified GWP thresholds, with site-safety exceptions.

Commission and Polish ministry guidance state that certification requirements now extend to relevant alternatives, including natural refrigerants, for stationary refrigeration, air-conditioning, and heat-pump work.

contrary_evidence: Equipment manufacturers and wholesalers may already remove non-compliant SKUs or provide their own selection rules.
Safety exceptions and equipment categories make a simple red-or-green decision potentially misleading.
Some restrictions concern placing equipment on the market rather than every installer quotation, weakening direct installer liability.

economics.acquisition_route: Demonstrate prevented quote errors in the family installer, then sell one white-label licence to a regional wholesaler before direct installer acquisition
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not evidence: 4,000 installer-equivalents at PLN 3,000 annual revenue plus several wholesaler licences yields roughly PLN 12m-16m revenue; at a 40% operating margin, seven mature years could produce PLN 20m-plus founder wealth
economics.founder_time: Two to three hours per day for product and data maintenance plus a scheduled weekly technical review with the pilot installer
economics.gross_margin_basis: A shared maintained rules graph can exceed 85% gross margin; catalogue cleanup, technical review, and wholesaler integration lower initial blended margin
economics.payback: Target one to six months depending on whether the first wholesaler funds integration; direct installer acquisition must remain self-serve
economics.pricing: Assumption: PLN 150-400 per installer per month or PLN 60,000-200,000 per wholesaler per year based on active contractor accounts and catalogues
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every quote invokes the rule set and catalogues and deadlines continue to change, creating recurring value if the checker is embedded before ordering

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A maintained SKU-to-refrigerant-to-ban graph with site exceptions, certification mappings, and observed quote corrections across wholesaler catalogues
fingerprint.customer: Polish HVAC and heat-pump installers, regional wholesalers, and renewable contractors configuring or servicing systems up to 12 kW
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: The family installer supplies the first workflow and error cases; one equipment wholesaler then embeds the API in its quote portal for portfolio distribution
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A mobile and API rules engine that reads model, refrigerant, capacity, system type, date, site-safety exception, and technician credentials; it flags eligibility, suggests permitted catalogue alternatives, and stores the decision record
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: A wholesaler pays an annual licence per active contractor, or an installer pays monthly, when model and site inputs are checked before the quote becomes a purchase order
fingerprint.problem_trigger: The 2024 F-gas regime introduced new refrigerant restrictions and certification scope, including service restrictions from 1 January 2026 and important GWP-based placing-on-market prohibitions for small heat pumps and air-conditioning equipment from 1 January 2027

founder_fit: The parents' renewable company is a direct pilot and domain-access advantage
Rules, product data, and exception analytics fit the founder's technical strengths
Wholesaler licensing can scale without thousands of installer meetings
A read-only quote checker is cheap and reversible before deeper commerce integration
risks: Incorrect refrigerant or safety guidance could contribute to an unsafe installation.
Incomplete SKU metadata can create false approvals or block valid equipment.
A wholesaler can internalise the rules after a pilot.
Maintaining cross-country rules may exceed a part-time founder's capacity without expert partners.

structure.commercial_archetype: White-label regulatory decision-rules API embedded in trade quoting
structure.control_point: The model-selection and purchase-order gate before an installer commits to equipment or service refrigerant
structure.critical_dependency: Complete manufacturer and wholesaler SKU metadata plus continuously correct interpretation of bans, safety exceptions, and Polish certification implementation

thesis: A refrigerant-aware rules plug-in can stop small HVAC and heat-pump installers from quoting a model that conflicts with upcoming placing-on-market bans, servicing restrictions, or technician certification scope. The scalable buyer may be a wholesaler that pays to embed the gate across contractor accounts; the founder's parents' renewable company provides a realistic installer pilot without turning the founder into a full-time trade consultant.
title: F-Gas Quote Gate for Heat-Pump Installers
uncertainties: The frequency and financial cost of real quote-selection errors must be measured in the family-company pilot.
Wholesaler willingness to expose catalogue metadata and pay for an external rules layer is unknown.
Polish transition arrangements for existing certificates and refresh training need current operational confirmation.
The 4,000-installer-equivalent wealth path is an unvalidated distribution scenario.
